## VaultKeeper.authorize() method

Decrypt a JWE, validate claims, verify executable identity, and return an opaque CapabilityToken.

**Signature:**

```typescript
authorize(jwe: string): Promise<{
        token: CapabilityToken;
        vaultResponse: VaultResponse;
    }>;
```

**Returns:**

Promise&lt;{ token: [CapabilityToken](./vaultkeeper.capabilitytoken.md)<!-- -->; vaultResponse: [VaultResponse](./vaultkeeper.vaultresponse.md)<!-- -->; }&gt;

Object containing an opaque [CapabilityToken](./vaultkeeper.capabilitytoken.md) for use with fetch/exec/getSecret, and a [VaultResponse](./vaultkeeper.vaultresponse.md) describing key status. When the JWE was decrypted with a non-current key, `vaultResponse.rotatedJwt` contains a re-encrypted JWE for the current key.

## Exceptions

[AuthorizationDeniedError](./vaultkeeper.authorizationdeniederror.md) If a new finite-use budget cannot be tracked because all accounting entries are still live.

## Remarks

Vault instances using the same loaded TypeScript module share in-memory accounting for up to 10,000 finite-use tokens. A tracked budget is retained through expiry. At capacity, a first finite-use authorization requires an expired entry to reclaim. Unlimited-use tokens need no entry. Expiry uses the latest wall-clock second observed by token enforcement, so a backward clock adjustment cannot make an expired token valid again. Each process maintains its own accounting.
